MARK 1220.title: Marketing and Society
MARK 1220.description: This course will challenge the dynamics of marketing and the role it plays within a social, sustainable and ethical context in various industries. Current social issues affecting marketing decisions within the context of business strategy will be explored. Students will understand the dynamics of marketing decision-making and the impact these decisions have on society's well-being with a focus on sustainability. Students should be able to: (i) appreciate the variety of social, political and economic forces affecting marketing organizations at the global and local level; (ii) identify/analyze current public issues in the interplay between marketing and society, such as advertising to children, addressing health and poverty issues, resource conservation, and climate change; (iii) critically evaluate the debates around the societal and ethical responsibilities of marketers; (iv) apply the above learning to real world cases. Students will gain the ability to apply basic theoretical and analytical frameworks to real world marketing problems and cases and reflect on their own behavior and experiences as consumers.
cilos: Identify and analyze current public issues in the interplay between marketing and society, such as social goods, health and poverty, resource conservation, climate change, consumerism, and conduct of societal marketing strategies and tactics

Identify, explain and evaluate the variety of social, political and economic forces affecting marketing organizations at the global and local level as the organization deals with its triple bottom-line objective benefits to the consumer, benefits to the company/ organization, and benefits to the society in general
Discuss ways in which the issue of environmental sustainability becomes part of a marketer’s positioning strategy
Critically evaluate the debates around the ethical and social responsibilities of marketers to fulfill the triple bottom-line objectives
Explain and discuss application of societal and sustainable marketing strategies in real world cases and situation

Discuss ways in which the issue of environmental sustainability becomes part of a marketer’s positioning strategy
Critically evaluate the debates around the ethical and social responsibilities of marketers to fulfill the triple bottom-line objectives
Explain and discuss application of societal and sustainable marketing strategies in real world cases and situation

MARK 1220.title: Marketing and Society
MARK 1220.description: This course will challenge the dynamics of marketing and the role it now plays within a social, sustainable and/or ethical context, in industries like Fashion, Food, Cigarettes and Alcohol, Social Media, NFT’s, E-Sports and Recycling. We explore and analyze current social issues affecting marketing decisions within the context of business strategy. This course aims to help students understand the dynamics of marketing decision-making and the impact these decisions have on society's well-being/"bad-being". Students should be able to: (i) appreciate the variety of social, political and economic forces affecting marketing organizations at the global and local level; (ii) identify/analyze current public issues in the interplay between marketing and society, such as advertising to children, junk food, and climate change; (iii) critically evaluate the debates around the ethical responsibilities of marketers; (iv) apply the above learning to real world cases. Students will gain the ability to apply basic theoretical and analytical frameworks to real world marketing problems and cases and reflect on their own behavior and experiences as consumers.
cilos: Identify and analyze current public issues in the interplay between marketing and society, such as fast fashion, junk food, and climate change
Identify, explain and evaluate the variety of social, political and economic forces affecting marketing organizations at the global and local level
Critically evaluate the debates around the ethical and social responsibilities of marketers
Apply the above learning to real world cases and situations

MARK 1230.title: Consumerism and Happiness
MARK 1230.description: We live in an age where consumption seems to be increasing without bounds, resulting in a consumeristic lifestyle. However, the question on whether increasing consumption results in happiness has remained very relevant with the passage of time. This course will examine the historical, cultural, psychological, religious, and economic perspectives on consumerism and the role of marketing in influencing a person’s self-identity and consumption attitudes. It will also examine how consumerism affects things that are important to many-- including personal finances, time with family and friends, the environment, and economic growth. The course will also look at how business, government and non-governmental organizations attempt to manage consumerism in their policies and strategies.
cilos: Identify and explain key societal and behavioral issues related to consumerism and happiness
Explain consumerism from different social scientific approaches
Make better decisions related to material possessions and personal finances
Explain how organizations may address the issue of consumerism in the conduct of their business

MARK 2120.title: Marketing Management
MARK 2120.description: Introduction to marketing from the perspective of the decision-maker; controllable variables (product, price, promotion and distribution), uncontrollable variables (competition, law, society, technology, and economy), consumer behavior and marketing research.
cilos: Acquire an understanding of basic marketing concepts.
Understand the strategic role of marketing.
Describe elements of the marketing mix and explain how they contribute to marketing strategy.
Identify and address the key decisions facing marketing managers.
Analyze market data to identify opportunities, Formulate market strategy, and interpret their implications for strategic planning.
Demonstrate a global outlook and an understanding of cultural diversity.
Apply business concepts and theories to make proper business decisions in real-life settings.

MARK 3220.title: Marketing Research
MARK 3220.description: Basic research tools and procedures used in marketing research, and strategic uses of marketing research information in managerial decision making.
cilos: Evaluate the effectiveness of marketing research in improving marketing outcomes and explain the role of marketing research in segmentation, targeting, positioning, and other marketing functions.
Describe the process of conducting a marketing research project.
Develop research skills to conduct common types of market research.

MARK 3410.title: Promotion and Advertising Management
MARK 3410.description: Major aspects of promotion, with emphasis on advertising: setting of advertising objectives, strategies, tactics, choice of media, budget determination and measuring advertising effectiveness.
cilos: Acquire an understanding of the marketing communication process.
Understand the role of promotion and advertising in strategic marketing.
Analyze and evaluate the key issues involved in planning and assessing integrated marketing communications strategies.
Apply the appropriate theories and tools to plan, develop, and evaluate marketing communications.
Design and implement a strategic marketing communication campaign through applied, hands-on experience.
Apply business concepts and theories in making proper business decisions in real-life Settings.

MARK 3420.title: Consumer Behavior
MARK 3420.description: Psychological concepts such as perception, learning and motivation, sociological concepts such as reference groups, family and culture and theories of purchase decision processes underlying consumer buying behavior.
cilos: Demonstrate a thorough understanding of the mental processes that guide consumer perceptions, attitudes, memory, and choices.
Analyze how these processes might differ as a consequence of social, cultural, and group influences.
Apply this knowledge to generate integrated and effective marketing strategies and tactics.
Forumulate recommendations if needed for public policy to protect consumer rights.

MARK 3430.title: Global Marketing
MARK 3430.description: Understanding the formulation of international/multinational marketing strategy; factors influencing international trade, assessment of market potential, threats and opportunities in the international market environment, global marketing activities.
cilos: Analyze the global business environment—including economic, cultural, and legal-political factors—and apply these insights to the development of effective marketing strategies and tactics.
Assess and address the needs of global consumers.
Demonstarte an ability to prepare go-to-market strategies for new markets.
Develop targeting and positioning strategies in a global environment.
Develop and formulate global marketing mix strategies and tactics.
Understand the challenges of marketing operations in emerging markets.
Comprehend the role and impact of sustainability on global marketing operations.

MARK 3460.title: Retail management in the digital age
MARK 3460.description: This course explores the critical concepts and strategies that define the modern retail landscape. It examines the impact of technology on retail operations, consumer behavior, and market dynamics. Students will learn about emerging trends such as e-commerce, mobile shopping, and data analytics, while also gaining insights into effective merchandising, customer engagement, and supply chain management. Through case studies, interactive discussions, and hands-on projects, students will develop the skills needed to thrive in a rapidly evolving retail environment and understand how to meet the demands of today's tech-savvy consumers.
cilos: Understand the concept of retailing from a customer-centric perspective.
Analyze customers’ shopping behavior to inform retail strategies.
Develop effective retailing strategies based on consumer buying motivations.
Evaluate key topics such as in-store space management, pricing, and promotion.

Gain insights relevant to careers in retail, wholesaling, manufacturing, advertising, and logistics. Explain and evaluate career opportunities in retail, wholesaling, manufacturing, advertising, and logistics.

Build a foundational knowledge of merchandising, pricing, promotion, and site selection in retailing. Describe and explain the fundamental concepts of merchandising, pricing and promotion in retailing.

MARK 3460.title: Retailing
MARK 3460.description: This course introduces the basic concept of retailing and its application in various retailing context. It will cover the major blocks of retailing, such as site-selection, display analysis, pricing and advertising strategies.
cilos: Understand the concept of retailing from a customer-centric perspective.
Analyze customers’ shopping behavior to inform retail strategies.
Develop effective retailing strategies based on consumer buying motivations.
Evaluate key topics such as in-store space management, pricing, and promotion.

Gain insights relevant to careers in retail, wholesaling, manufacturing, advertising, and logistics. Explain and evaluate career opportunities in retail, wholesaling, manufacturing, advertising, and logistics.

Build a foundational knowledge of merchandising, pricing, promotion, and site selection in retailing. Describe and explain the fundamental concepts of merchandising, pricing and promotion in retailing.

MARK 3480.title: Pricing Strategy
MARK 3480.description: This course is designed to deepen understanding of pricing issues which marketing managers may face under some degree of market power.  The course will develop basic pricing theories and concepts from economics and marketing and present managerial implications for decision making.
cilos: Apply the Value Based Pricing Framework to formulate pricing decisions.
Understand how to estimate consumers’ willingness to pay and its role in pricing decisions.
Explain the impact of psychological factors on consumers’ willingness to pay.
Understand the role of price segmentation in developing pricing strategies, such as promotions, versioning, bundling, and subscriptions.
Understand the role and effectiveness of innovative pricing strategies, such as revenue management, freemiums, and online auctions.
Understand the role of ethics and legal issues in pricing decisions.

MARK 3510.title: Business to Business Marketing
MARK 3510.description: The fundamental character of business markets and the decision-making nature of organizational customers; different approaches to business marketing, as typified in the relationships between buyers and sellers, and built around the concept of value; current trends changing the face of business-to-business marketing; critical analysis and problem-solving with respect to business market management.
cilos: Understand the nature, structure, and distinguishing characteristics of business-to-business markets.
Develop and apply a framework to analyse organizational buying behavior across commercial, enterprises (large and small) as well as government, and institutional buyers.
Apply demand analysis and segmentation techniques to the business market.
Develop effective sales and marketing strategies and tactics in product and service management, pricing, promotion, distribution, and sales to take advantage of business marketing opportunities.

MARK 3610.title: Digital Marketing
MARK 3610.description: Digital Marketing has reshaped the consumer landscape, and it is offering business new challenges and opportunities. In this course, students will learn important concepts related to digital marketing, factors that facilitate effective digital marketing initiative, and a consumer-centric approach to develop marketing plans. Students will also have hands-on experiences with web analytics and other real-life examples.
cilos: Develop theoretical basis for digital consumer behavior.
Understand the key characteristics digital environment to develop insights for yourself as a marketer, but also as a consumer.
Acquire hands-on experience using web analytics tools for data-driven marketing.
Develop skills to visualize and present analytical results.
Learn how to develop a digital marketing strategy based on real-life examples.
Familiarize yourself to opportunities and challenges offered by new marketing channels.
Utilize generative AI and latest technology for marketing campaigns.

MARK 3620.title: Marketing Analytics
MARK 3620.description: This course develops the foundation and integrated framework for understanding marketing analytics. It introduces major applications of data analytics in marketing, including customer analytics, product analytics, pricing analytics, and advertising analytics.
cilos: Understand why and where marketing analytics are needed.
Understand basic and some advanced regression methods.
Understand basic principles of predictive models.
Understand principles and practices of field experiments.
Familiarize basic applications related customer, advertising, product, and pricing.

MARK 4210.title: Strategic Marketing
MARK 4210.description: Developing a comprehensive and integrated framework for directing and managing the marketing functions of a company; methods to analyze marketing opportunities, assess competitive advantages and forecast market changes.
cilos: Apply the key concepts and theoretical frameworks, and practical knowledge, to solve marketing problems using both qualitative and quantitative analyses.
Criticially think and evaluate the challenges to make strategic marketing decisions.

MARK 4290.title: Special Topics
MARK 4290.description: Selected topics in current marketing thought and practices; topics vary from semester to semester.
cilos: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.

MARK 4450.title: Brand Management
MARK 4450.description: This course is designed to help students develop a practical understanding of the tools, rules, and strategies of brand management.  By the end of the semester, students will be able to assess critical aspects of a branding strategy such as: how to introduce and name new products; how to interpret brand performance; and how to manage a brand over time, product categories, and geographical markets.  MARK 4450 is intended for individuals considering careers at senior levels of corporate management or as consultants in strategy firms, ad agencies, and market research companies.
cilos: Assess critical aspects of brand management.
Design brand positioning strategies.
Generate brand resonance.
Evaluate appropriate brand elements.
Leverage secondary brand associations.
Manage a brand over time and across various geographical markets.

MARK 4980.title: Independent Study
MARK 4980.description: Directed study of selected problems in marketing not covered in other courses. May be repeated for credits if different topics are taken.
cilos: Demonstrate an in-depth and substantial knowledge and understanding on the topic chosen for the independent study.
Apply suitable business theories and framework to analyze and evaluate data relevant to the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.

MARK 5100.title: Customer Relationship Management
MARK 5100.description: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is a strategic approach that businesses use to manage interactions with current and potential customers. In today’s competitive market, fostering strong customer relationships enhances loyalty and retention, directly impacting revenue growth. In this course, students will (1) learn the domains of strategic, operational and analytic CRM; (2) be able to create a CRM plan for businesses; and (3) be capable of objectively critiquing CRM programs.
cilos: Understand the history of CRM and see the evolution and progression.
Understand and identify the three different spheres of CRM and their objectives, including strategic, operational, and analytical spheres.
Create a realistic and viable CRM plan for businesses.
Gain enough insight into this functional specialty of marketing so that they may in the future choose this area of specialization if desired.
Develop a solid foundation of critical working knowledge of each CRM sphere: strategic, operational, analytical.
Gain a broad and deep understanding of the power generated by information/data to change behavior, particularly as it relates to customer retention.
Objectively critique CRM programs and judge their probability of success/failure.

MARK 5110.title: Content Marketing
MARK 5110.description: Content marketing is a strategic marketing approach focused on creating and distributing valuable, relevant, and consistent content to attract and retain a clearly defined audience - and, ultimately, to drive profitable customer action. This course will look at content marketing strategy and execution from a holistic perspective, as a journey that includes an understanding of all the content brands are creating, from paid channels, earned channels to owned channels - TV commercials, brand websites, campaigns and events, company social media accounts, E-commerce flagship stores, etc. This course aims to bring students to the real marketing world.
cilos: Understand what content marketing is.
Be familiar with the key steps to develop content marketing executions.
Develop the channel-specific content strategy and execution.
Develop the consumer journey stage-specific content strategy and execution.
Apply the principles to evaluate and comment on content development outputs.
Be prepared for the future of content marketing.

MARK 5120.title: Marketing Strategy
MARK 5120.description: Strategic marketing objectives and implementation of strategies through pricing, distribution channels, promotion and new-product decisions.  This is a core course for MBA.
cilos: Conduct a marketing environmental analysis and identify market opportunities that will be strategically fit with the company or organization.
Identify and evaluate segments, and decide on the appropriate target(s) within a given market.
Construct a persuasive value proposition and positioning statement for a given offering.
Formulate marketing strategies and make strategic marketing decisions, including specific marketing mix strategies.
Monitor and control strategic marketing plans.
Make effective presentations of a company’s or organization’s marketing plan.

MARK 5220.title: The Art of War and Eastern Wisdom in Business Competition
MARK 5220.description: This course aims to explore and integrate the ancient Eastern wisdom into modern Western management science and apply to modern business competition. To achieve this goal, this course will use Sun Tzu's "The Art of War" as a vehicle to introduce the foundation of Eastern wisdom (Confucianism, Taoism, Buddhism) to management executives. Sun Tzu's "The Art of War " has proved to be a classic work on strategy, applicable to both military and business situation. This course is to crystallize some concepts and ideas put forth in "The Art of War" into a few business strategic principles and an innovative framework of 4Stop so that these can be more easily understood and applied.
cilos: Identify the profound wisdom of the East and the competitive edge strategic thinking.
Integrate the ancient Eastern Wisdom into modern Western management science.
Apply the wisdom of the East into daily life and into any competitive environment.

MARK 5260.title: Luxury Strategy
MARK 5260.description: This intensive block week course addresses the unique properties, opportunities, and challenges of the luxury industry by studying issues relevant to the field in the various aspects of the business, from production and management to distribution and promotion. Students will have the unique opportunity to interact with senior executives from a renowned luxury brand as they feedback on students' research and recommendations, and guide them to understand their brand strategy and implementation.
cilos: Recognize the unique properties, opportunities and challenges of the luxury industry.
Identify and analyze key issues specific to the luxury industry.
Apply marketing knowledge and strategy to solve issues at hand.

MARK 5275.title: Retailing
MARK 5275.description: This course discusses the retailing strategies that aim to foster a long-term win-win situation that benefits all players in the marketplace - consumers, retailers and manufactures. The primary focus of this course will be on understanding customers’ shopping behavior and developing retailing strategy with the understanding of why and how consumers buy. The topics we will cover provide a firm foundation in many dimensions of retailing, including merchandising, pricing, promotion and customer relationship management.
cilos: Identify the needs of consumers based on an in-depth understanding of their buying behavior.
Develop the market positioning of the retailer based on the analysis of the market environment and the preferences of target consumers.
Develop skills to build retailer brands that will prosper in the global marketplace.
Develop and implement retailing strategies in the digital marketplace.
Develop sustainable retailing strategies and develop a sense of social responsibility as a future market leader.

MARK 5290.title: Understanding Consumers
MARK 5290.description: This course combines an in-depth exploration of consumer psychology with elements of advertising and marketing research, with the goal of enhancing students' understanding of marketing tactics and strategy.
cilos: Identify key principles and concepts relating to consumer behavior.
Examine the available theory and research concerning the psychology of the consumer.
Design and develop an effective marketing mix for a product or service relying on in-depth knowledge of the consumers.

MARK 5300.title: Pricing Strategy
MARK 5300.description: Students can learn practical tools to design pricing strategies from a marketing perspective and considers economic, strategic and psychological inputs in pricing decisions that are sustainable and generate profitable revenue streams. Through examples and case studies, it discusses the tools to assess consumer’s willingness to pay, and how this information can be used to improve pricing strategies. Other popular and innovative pricing tactics, such as customization, bundling, subscriptions, versioning, freemium, online auctions and revenue management will also be covered.
cilos: Apply the basic pricing frameworks in a competitive environment.
Design to derive consumers' willingness to pay and its role in pricing decisions.
Explain the impact of psychological factors on consumers' willingness to pay.
Recognize the role of ethics and legal issues in pricing decisions.

MARK 5310.title: Applied Marketing Research for Managers
MARK 5310.description: Methods of structuring, analyzing and measuring major classes of marketing problems; quantitative aspects of demand, consumer reaction to product characteristics, advertising effectiveness, effectiveness of competitors' strategies.
cilos: Translate management problems into tangible research questions.
Evaluate marketing research and identify the opportunities and potential limitations of it.
Design and implement a marketing research project.

MARK 5330.title: Brand Management
MARK 5330.description: The course provides students with an understanding of what brand equity is and then uses a structured approach for managing and leveraging it to gain competitive advantage. The emphasis is on actual decisions a manager makes and the long-term effects of these marketing actions on brand equity. Cases are used to demonstrate common types of pitfalls that must be avoided in order to build brand equity.
cilos: Understand why brands matter
Develop successful brand development strategies
Measure and track brand performance
Configure brand architectures
Implement branding strategies through the marketing mix
Design strategies to grow and sustain brands

MARK 5380.title: Mastering D2C Marketing
MARK 5380.description: This course will present an in-depth analysis of digital/direct marketing, focusing primarily on the scientific foundations upon which this marketing discipline is built. Attention will be on various formulae that are used to predict probability of response, forecast potential profit, and inform testing and campaigning. Students will also learn the critical ingredients for success within developing creative positions and creating offers. The specific differences between digital/direct marketing and general marketing/advertising will also be highlighted.
cilos: Apply the various scientific formulae that form the foundation for digital/direct marketing, including predicting the probability of response.
Analyze and plan media in a marketing environment.
Create a strategic marketing plan for a digital/direct marketing campaign.
Gain insight into this functional specialty of marketing.
Lay a solid foundation of critical knowledge to pursue a career in marketing.
Gain a broad, and deep understanding of the power generated by media alone to change behavior, particularly as it relates to customer acquisition and retention.
Objectively critique digital/direct marketing campaigns/executions and judge their probability of success/failure.
Understand the best application of market research to digital/direct marketing campaigns.

MARK 5390.title: Global Marketing
MARK 5390.description: We live in a dynamic, global marketplace. This course aims to introduce students to the essentials of global marketing management. We look at how global customers and firms behave and operate in the global marketplace as well as the strategies and tactics marketers can use to operate successfully in this global environment.
cilos: Assess market opportunities and challenges in the global marketplace.
Assess and address needs of global consumers.
Develop global marketing mix strategies.
Understand the nuances of marketing in emerging markets.
Comprehend the role and impact of sustainability on global marketing operations.
Appreciate the importance of being sensitive to the marketing environment of the host country.

MARK 5400.title: Marketing Analytics
MARK 5400.description: The course will introduce the foundation of marketing analytics. It will first draw upon economics and marketing theories to understand why and where analytics are needed to solve marketing problems, and then introduce major applications, including customer analytics, product analytics, pricing analytics, and advertising analytics. The focus will be on the business logics and methodological principles behind the common applications.
cilos: Understand why and where marketing analytics are needed.
Learn basic and some advanced regression methods.
Understand basic principles of predictive models.
Learn the principles of experimental method.
Understand basic applications like customer analytics, advertising analytics, product analytics, and pricing analytics.

MARK 5410.title: Seminar in Quantitative Modeling
MARK 5410.description: Overview of the literature on modeling marketing phenomena.
cilos: Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.
Integrate functional knowledge to solve marketing-related problems.

MARK 5420.title: Behavioral Decision Theory
MARK 5420.description: This course is designed to familiarize students with a wide variety of issues related to consumer judgment and decision making. In addition to providing students with basic knowledge on behavioral decision theory, this course will provide rigorous training to students to generate their own research ideas that lead to projects that are doable and worth doing. The readings will be from Consumer Behavior/Marketing as well as the basic disciplines of Economics and Psychology.
cilos: Recognize a wide variety of issues related to consumer judgment and decision making.
Generate students’ own research ideas that lead to projects that are doable and worth doing.
Generate interesting questions about consumer decision making.

MARK 5430.title: Digital Marketing
MARK 5430.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the concepts and skills essential in digital marketing. This course focuses on the decisions that managers make and the tools that they use to support an effective digital marketing strategy. We try to answer questions such as the following: What is digital marketing? What makes for a good digital marketing strategy and what new tools can be used in digital marketing practice?
cilos: Gain digital consumer insights and solve real life digital marketing problems by analyzing digital marketing data, applying digital marketing tools, and developing a holistic digital marketing framework.
Provide segmentation, targeting, positioning, and branding strategy as a manager of digital marketing. Develop digital marketing plans based on the marketing environment.

Build brands that will prosper in the digital global marketplace. Skills include brand communication, social media planning, digital message strategy, public relations, crisis management, and brand research.
Develop and implement digital marketing strategies, including various pricing tools, product decisions, digital promotion strategy, online and offline channel coordination.

Create sustainable digital marketing strategies and develop a sense of social responsibility in the digital environment. Topics include consumer welfare, data privacy, online marketing fraud, digital green marketing.

MARK 5470.title: Seminar in Consumer Behavior II
MARK 5470.description: Overview of advanced topics in psychology and consumer behavior research. An information processing approach is used to help students develop expertise on a range of diverse topics such as attitude formation and change, culture, information processing, motivation and goals, emotion, consumer decision making.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Design research to solve marketing-related problems in an innovative fashion that applies their specialized knowledge.

MARK 5500.title: Sustainable Marketing
MARK 5500.description: These days a critical question in companies’ boardrooms is no longer whether to become a good corporate citizen but how. Corporate social responsibility and sustainability have never been more prominent on corporate agendas than today. Marketing plays a vital role in sustainability. In this course, we explore the meaning of sustainability in a marketing context and how marketing can create value in such endeavors.
cilos: Understand what constitutes environmental and social sustainability.
Comprehend why sustainable marketing is vitally important both to society and to a successful business strategy.
Understand how sustainability can drive a successful marketing strategy from the mission statement down to the strategy development and implementation.
See what drives consumer activism and what strategies companies can deploy to cope with consumer boycotts.
Grasp how sustainability can inform and improve marketing practices as an integral part of a competitive marketing plan.

MARK 5520.title: Experimental Design and Analysis for Behavioral Research
MARK 5520.description: This course is aimed at PhD students who intent to conduct experimental and quasi-experimental research in business (e.g., marketing, organizational behavior).  The primary objective is to master the concepts and tools needed for collecting and analyzing behavioral data.  In addition, the course provides an introduction to SAS, one of the most widely used statistical programming languages for manipulating and analyzing data.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Design research to solve marketing-related problems in an innovative fashion that applies their specialized knowledge.
Present their discipline knowledge, teach independent courses, and/or lead discussion sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

MARK 5530.title: Navigating Business Decisions with Data and Causality
MARK 5530.description: This course aims to teach students basic conceptions and methods for conducting causal estimations in business problems. The course will cover classical causal inference framework, and different methodologies that could be used in various settings, including randomized, quasi-, and natural experiments, and observation data.
cilos: Understand some common applications of causal inference in business problems.
Evaluate the validity and value of an experiment for causal analysis.
Collect appropriate observational data sets for causal analysis.
Design rigorous experiments to properly measure the causal impact of a given policy.
Identify appropriate methodology for conducting causal estimates using a given dataset and context.
Avoid expensive mistakes in their research work by using appropriate experimental design or methodologies.
Derive valuable insights from their causal research to improve business decision making.

MARK 5540.title: New Product Development Using Design Thinking
MARK 5540.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of how to apply design thinking principles and methodologies to the new product development (NPD) process. Students will learn the NPD process steps and concepts of design thinking including human-centered design, rapid prototyping, and creative problem solving. Through a combination of theoretical knowledge, practical case studies, and industry insights, students will develop the skills and expertise needed to lead new product development projects, navigate global business challenges, and drive sustainable growth through innovation.
cilos: Apply the New Product Development (NPD) and design thinking processes to create innovative, user-centered, and market-viable products.
Use ideation, prototyping, and testing techniques to develop and refine product concepts based on real user insights.
Lead and collaborate in cross-functional teams to integrate design thinking into business strategy and innovation practices.

MARK 5560.title: Marketing Communication
MARK 5560.description: Marketing communication is a part of the marketing mix that establishes and builds relationships with the market through directly or indirectly --- informing, persuading, and reminding customers about their offering. This course is designed to help students develop an integrated marketing communication plan and evaluate its effectiveness.
cilos: Explain the importance of marketing communication in marketing strategy.
Discuss the communication process to the core customers by establishing points of parity and points of differentiation for the brand.
Present the important issues in planning and evaluating integrated marketing communication.
Apply the appropriate marketing framework, theories and tools to plan, develop, and evaluate marketing communications.
Propose a complete marketing communication campaign.

MARK 5577.title: Business to Business Marketing
MARK 5577.description: A comprehensive approach to Business to Business (B2B) marketing that includes specific practical applications as well as theoretical constructs necessary for successful outcomes in the B2B space. The course includes case studies, outside reading, and a group project requiring students to submit a B2B marketing plan for approval, giving students a real-world experience. Throughout the course, the emphasis is on current global best practices.
cilos: Enumerate and explain fully the key differences between Business to Consumer (B2C) and Business to Business (B2B) marketing.
Describe in detail the functions and roles of each actor in the Decision-Making Unit (DMU).
Quantify the importance and placement of ESG/DEI in B2B marketing.
Evaluate and quantify the role and significance of personal selling in B2B markets.
Create targeted communications strategy and tactics.
Execute pricing strategies and practices in B2B marketing.

MARK 5588.title: Entrepreneurial Marketing
MARK 5588.description: In the last decade, we have seen a significant increase in the number of startups being founded globally with their biggest challenges being growth and expansion. In this course, students will learn how to think entrepreneurially when it comes to marketing. The course will discuss topics such as business planning, building brand awareness and growth using strategic and innovative marketing approach. Whether students are looking to start their own business, join a startup, or join a corporation that values an intrapreneurial spirit, this course will teach them the essentials/basics they need to succeed.
cilos: Understand what is entrepreneurship: launching and working at a startup – the opportunities and challenges.
Assess market opportunities and challenges in the global marketplace.
Build a strategic, scalable and sustainable marketing journey.
Use technology to build a sustainable and eco-friendly footprint.
Understand how marketing software (AI and data analytics) can enable quicker growth.

MARK 5688.title: Marketing Strategy Simulation
MARK 5688.description: This course draws upon knowledge participants acquired from various marketing courses. The course adopts an experiential learning approach using a marketing business simulation, a learning-by-doing mindset. Students will come as close to a real-world business environment as they can get in a classroom setting. Students will play the role of a marketing team of a firm and compete against other teams making a variety of marketing strategic and tactical decisions. Teams will have to develop a comprehensive, workable and successful marketing strategy, making use of a wide variety of marketing analytical tools to guide their environmental analysis and decision making. The simulation will stretch over several rounds. The course will be complemented with case analyses related to the topics covered in the simulation.
cilos: Understand and know how to use marketing analytical tools.
Develop marketing strategies.
Realize the importance and possible impact of the external environment.
Develop a long-term thinking mindset.
Look at the “big picture” instead of being short-sighted.

MARK 5689.title: Public Relations
MARK 5689.description: This course aims to equip students with the skills to integrate public relations (PR) into marketing strategies. The course covers definitions, history, processes, writing skills, media relations, digital PR, crisis communication, and integration with marketing, which equips students to develop a comprehensive PR plan.
cilos: Understand the principles of public relations.
Know how to develop strategies and messaging.
Have a working knowledge of the key elements of PR (e.g., writing, digital, crisis management etc.).
Create a PR plan that effectively integrates into a marketing plan.
Demonstrate awareness of trends, issues, and complexities in PR.

MARK 5700.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing
MARK 5700.description: This course will give students a high-level overview of Artificial Intelligence technologies, concepts, and business use cases related to Marketing. After the course, students will be able to identify and leverage AI to enhance and/or disrupt business models both within marketing functions and on a larger organizational level. We will also devote part of the course to explore how careers of marketing professionals may change in the future because of AI and get students to think about their professional development in a world where AI and human beings will inevitably work together.
cilos: Build an understanding of the fundamental branches of AI and their applications in marketing.
Gain the ability to select what type of AI may be applicable to specific business use cases.
Develop an appreciation for the potential risks and ethical issues involved with the proliferation of AI in marketing and business in general.
Identify business skillsets and personal development goals which will allow them to adapt to jobs of the future in marketing.

MARK 5710.title: Analytical Modeling in Marketing
MARK 5710.description: This course provides Marketing MPhil/PhD students with foundational knowledge in quantitative marketing, with a focus on analytical modeling. It will cover a range of theoretical topics including pricing, advertising, two-sided markets, consumer search and learning, and information design.
cilos: Understand basic marketing theories.
Develop intuitions for important models.
Evaluate research papers with analytical models.

MARK 6510.title: Current Topics in Consumer Research
MARK 6510.description: Advanced seminar covering current research and theory in consumer behavior and marketing. Topics will vary with the term, but may include areas related to consumer judgment and decision processes, attitude formation and change, reactions to advertising, consumer information procession, affective, motivational and cognitive determinants of consumer behavior, and cultural and individual differences in consumer behavior. May be repeated for credit. Graded P or F.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

MARK 6900-6910.title: Special Topics
MARK 6900-6910.description: Study of selected areas in marketing knowledge and thought; topics may vary by term; individual projects and reports.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

MARK 6950.title: Marketing Action Learning Project
MARK 6950.description: A team project that focuses on analyzing and solving a real-world marketing challenge within an organization (e.g., company, NGO). Students will develop marketing consulting experience, collaborate to produce a marketing report, and present their in-depth insights and recommended solutions to the sponsor.
cilos: Identify marketing opportunities and challenges
Gather in-depth consumer and market insights
Come up with effective marketing recommendations
Sharpen their team-work and communication skills
Develop marketing strategies and tactical solutions based on market intelligence

MARK 6960-6970.title: Independent Study
MARK 6960-6970.description: Study of selected marketing issues under the supervision of a faculty member. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

MARK 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
MARK 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.
Design research to solve marketing-related problems in an innovative fashion that applies their specialized knowledge.
Present their discipline knowledge and lead discussion sessions effectively.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

MARK 7900.title: Doctoral Seminar
MARK 7900.description: This seminar focuses on special topics in marketing; possible topics are measurement and structural equation modeling, agency theory, channel structures, diffusion modeling, group decision making, information processing, attribution theory, philosophy of science and categorization theory.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to explain specific areas in the marketing literature in order to differentiate and critique the literature.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.

MARK 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
MARK 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.

Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of problems in the field of marketing in order to propose solutions.
